THE SELLER agrees to sell to the PURCHASER who agrees to purchase the following property (hereinafter called "the property") upon the following terms and conditions:

1.	THE PROPERTY

ERF _______, KNYSNA, in the Province of the Western Cape, situated at ____________________________________________, Knysna, measuring _______ square metres in extent and held under Title Deed No ______________________________.

2.	PURCHASE PRICE

2.1	The purchase price payable by the PURCHASER to the SELLER for the property is R__________ (___________________________________ Rand) and shall be payable to the SELLER on registration of transfer of the property into the name of the PURCHASER, to be secured by :

2.2	a deposit of R___________ (___________________________________________ Rand) payable within 7 (Seven) working days of acceptance hereof, which amount is to be paid in cash to the SELLER's Conveyancer; and which amounts shall be invested by the SELLER's Conveyancers in an interest-bearing account until transfer, the interest earned thereon to accrue to the PURCHASER. 

2.3	the balance on or before the _________________________ by issue of a guarantee by a bank or financial institution acceptable to the SELLER’s Conveyancer. In the event of this agreement being subject to the fulfillment of a suspensive condition(s) such guarantee shall be furnished within 14 (Fourteen) days of fulfillment of such condition(s).

3.	COSTS

The PURCHASER shall pay all transfer costs incurred to enable registration of transfer of the property into his name, including Transfer Duty which amounts shall be paid upon request of the SELLER's Conveyancers.

4.	TRANSFER & RISK

	Transfer of the property shall be passed by the SELLER's Conveyancers and shall be given and taken on _____________________________ or as soon as is reasonably possible thereafter.  Both parties shall sign all transfer documents on request by SELLER’s Conveyancers.  The property shall remain at the risk of the SELLER until the date of transfer from which date the property shall be at the sole risk of the PURCHASER. Furthermore, the Seller and the Purchaser undertake to comply with the Financial Intelligent Centre Act No.38 of 2001, providing all documents as required, when called upon to do so by the Conveyancer and the Agent.

5.	POSSESSION & OCCUPATION

5.1	The PURCHASER shall take vacant occupation and possession of the property on ________________________________________ into his name. 

5.2	Should the date of occupation not coincide with the date of transfer, the occupant shall monthly in advance pay to the owner, occupational rental in the sum of R ___________ (________________________________________ Rand) per month for the period of occupation, or pro-rata thereof if applicable.  The occupant shall, during such occupation, be responsible for the cost of all utility bills, including electricity, water, gas (if applicable) and internet etc and shall keep the Property, including garden and pool, in a neat and well-maintained condition.  Should the occupant be the PURCHASER, occupation will only be given once the PURCHASER has performed all his contractual obligations, including but not limited to, payment of transfer and bond costs, signature of transfer and bond documents (if applicable) and payment of occupational rental as agreed.

5.3	Should the occupant be the PURCHASER, he shall not be entitled to effect any alterations in respect of the Property without the prior, written consent of the SELLER. 

5.4	In the event of this agreement being cancelled for any reason whatsoever and the PURCHASER has taken early occupation; the PURCHASER will vacate the Property immediately and return the Property to the SELLER in the same condition.

5.5	Occupation shall, by operation of law, be subject to the existing lease in respect of the property, a copy of which the PURCHASER acknowledges to have in his possession.

5.6	The Purchaser shall be obliged, in the event of cancellation of this Agreement to vacate the Property within (7) Seven days of written request by the Conveyancer to do so, it being expressly agreed between the parties that no tenancy shall be created by virtue of the Purchaser taking occupation of the property prior to registration of transfer.

6.	RATES AND CHARGES

The SELLERS authorise the Conveyancer to obtain a municipal clearance certificate from the municipality including any possible historical debt due and payable to the municipality as required in terms of Section 118(1) and 118(3) of the Municipal Systems Act 32 of 2000. The Conveyancer shall determine from the municipal rates assessment form if there are any such arrear rates and taxes due to the municipality and shall obtain an instruction from the SELLERS to settle these arrears. 

The PURCHASERS shall be liable for the payment of any Local Authority Rates and other charges, including any levies, in respect of the property beyond the date of Transfer and Registration.  

7.	DEFAULT / BREACH

Should any Party to this agreement (‘the defaulting party’) breach any of his obligations under this Agreement (which shall include the signature of any documentation relating to the passing of transfer or the payment of any amount due under this agreement or the delivery of the guarantee referred to above) and remain in breach thereof after the expiry of a period of Seven (7) days’ notice in writing, given to the defaulting party by the non-defaulting party or on his behalf calling upon the defaulting party to remedy such breach the non-defaulting party shall have the right, without prejudice to any other rights to which he may be entitled in law or under this Agreement namely:-  EITHER

7.1	to hold the defaulting party bound to this Agreement, to enforce performance of the obligations of the defaulting party hereunder and (if applicable) to claim immediate payment of all amounts payable by the defaulting party under this Agreement, including (if applicable) payment of the full balance of the purchase price outstanding together with any default interest accruing thereon, costs and other charges; OR 

7.2	to cancel this Agreement forthwith; and

7.2.1	to retake possession of the property, the PURCHASER hereby waiving any lien for improvements which he may have over the property; and

7.2.2	to claim damages from the defaulting party in which event, if the PURCHASER is the defaulting party, the SELLER shall not be obliged to return to the PURCHASER such amounts as have already been paid by the PURCHASER, but shall be entitled to retain such amounts, together with interest accruing thereon, until such dispute, if any, has been settled.

8.	BOND 

8.1	This Agreement of Sale is subject to the PURCHASER within 30 (THIRTY) days of acceptance, being granted a loan by a South African Bank or financial institution in the amount of R___________ (_________________________________________________________________ Rand) or such lesser amount as the PURCHASER may, in writing, accept; the repayment of which loan may be required by such lending bank or similar financial institution, to be secured by the registration of a mortgage bond over the property simultaneously with transfer thereof to the PURCHASER.  The aforesaid date shall be automatically extended by a further 30 (THIRTY) days if required.  This condition shall be deemed to have been fulfilled upon the issue to the PURCHASER by the said bank or financial institution of a written quotation and a written pre-agreement statement as contemplated in section 92 of the National Credit Act No. 34 of 2005 in respect of the loan in the said amount within the period referred to in this paragraph, whether or not such quotation or pre-agreement statement is accepted by the PURCHASER.

8.2	The PURCHASER acknowledges that the PURCHASER is aware that the granting of credit is subject to costs and charges levied in terms of the National Credit Act.

9.	COMMISSION

9.1	Commission is payable by the SELLER and is calculated at ____% of the Purchase Price plus VAT.  Such commission shall be due on fulfilment of the suspensive conditions herein and payable upon Transfer and Registration of transfer of the property into the name of the PURCHASER. The SELLER hereby irrevocably instructs the Conveyancers to pay the commission amount to Dream Knysna (Pty) Limited as first draw against the proceeds of the sale.   

9.2	The PURCHASER warrants and undertakes to the SELLER that the PURCHASER has not been introduced to the property by any third party entitled to commission other than the agent/s specified in this Agreement on Page 2 of the CONTRACT INFORMATION.

10	GENERAL CONDITIONS

10.1	The property is sold, as regards its extent, as set out in the title deed(s) thereof, and the SELLER shall not be liable in respect of any shortfall and shall have no claim in respect of any excess which may be found on re-survey of the property.

10.2	The PURCHASER acknowledges that he has satisfied himself by personal inspection, or by means of independent sources of information, concerning any burdens or servitudes to which the property may be subject, and also concerning all advantages and disadvantages attaching to the property; and hereby agrees that the SELLER shall not be liable to him/her in respect of any failure by the SELLER or his Agent to inform him of any such qualities.

10.3	The SELLER gives no express or implied warranty whatsoever with respect to the property or any aspect thereof.  Moreover, the property is sold "voetstoots" as it now lies, with any patent or latent defects to which it may be subject.

10.4	The PURCHASER acknowledges that he has not been influenced into entering into this Agreement by any express or implied information, statement or representation given or made by or on behalf of the SELLER; the PURCHASER hereby waives in favour of the SELLER any rights whatsoever which he otherwise may have obtained against the SELLER as result of any such information, statement or representation given or made by or on behalf of the SELLER.

10.5	This Deed of Sale constitutes the entire Agreement between the parties, and no other conditions, stipulations, warranties or representatives whatsoever have been made by either party or his agent other than such as are contained herein.  No modification, variation or alteration hereto shall be valid unless in writing and signed by both parties or their respective agents.

10.6	Any latitude which may have been allowed by the SELLER in respect of any breach by the PURCHASER in terms hereof, shall not under any circumstances be deemed to be a waiver of the SELLER's rights under this agreement nor a novation hereof, nor shall it prevent the SELLER from exercising any right nor absolve the PURCHASER from any obligation under this Agreement.

10.7	Should there be more than one PURCHASER, their liability in terms of this agreement shall be joint and several.

10.8	As per Requirements by Law, the SELLER and PURCHASER warrant that they are aware of their obligations in terms of the Financial Intelligence Centre Act and shall produce all necessary documents to comply with this Act to the Agent and Conveyancer.

10.9	As per SARS Declaration, the SELLER and PURCHASER warrant and confirm to each other and the Estate Agent, that they have met all their tax obligations and commitments to the South African Receiver of Revenue Services, whether in their personal capacity or otherwise. Should the transfer be delayed or cancelled as a result of this breach of warrantee, the defaulting party will be liable for all costs incurred and damages suffered by the aggrieved party in accordance with the Breach Clause above.

10.10	The SELLER and PURCHASER hereby give their consent to Dream Knysna (Pty) Limited and the Conveyancing Attorneys, who will register the transfer of the property, to process their personal information for all purposes and requirements that are specifically related to this sale in accordance with the Provisions of the Protection of the Personal Information Act (“POPIA”).

10.11	The SELLER hereby warrants that he, to the best of his knowledge, is not aware of any invasive species of vegetation and plant life, as prescribed in the Regulations of the NEMBA Act (Act 10 of 2004), on the Property and that he is    not in possession of any valid permit to keep any such species on the Property.

10.12	Dream Knysna (Pty) Limited are hereby authorised to erect a SOLD board on the Property for a period of three months period after selling the property. 

10.13 In this Agreement words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, words importing the masculine gender shall include the female gender and vice versa.

11.	COSTS OF ENFORCEMENT OF SELLER’S AND PURCHASER’S RIGHTS

If for any reason whatsoever  any party instructs his attorneys to take action against the other party in terms hereof, and notwithstanding that such action may not involve litigation or the issue of process from any court of law, then the party that is in breach shall be liable for, and the innocent party shall be entitled to recover on demand, all such legal fees incurred by such party including in particular wasted costs of transfer, collection costs and all costs on an attorney/client scale, notwithstanding that, in the absence of this paragraph, the innocent party would not be entitled to recover any costs from the party in breach, or costs other than on a party and party scale.

12.	NOTICES AND DOMICILIA

The Parties to the Agreement choose their respective domicilia citandi et executandi for all purposes arising hereunder and as their respective addresses for the service of any notices required to be served upon them at the addresses detailed on Page 2 “Contract Information”.

12.1	Any notice or communication required or permitted in terms of this Agreement shall be valid and effective only if in writing, but it shall be competent to give such notice by email.

	12.2	Either party may, by notice to the other, change the physical address chosen as his domicilium, or may advise via email; provided that such change[s] shall only become effective on the sixth business day after the date of receipt, or deemed date of receipt, of such notice by the addressee.

12.3 	Any notice to a party shall –

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein contained a written notice or communication actually received by a party to this Agreement shall be an adequate written notice or communication to him/her notwithstanding that it was not sent to or delivered at the chosen domicilium citandi et executandi or sent via email address as stipulated herein.

13.	EXPIRY

The first signature to this agreement shall constitute an irrevocable offer, which may not be withdrawn prior to presentation to the SELLER or the PURCHASER, whichever the case may be, and which thereafter shall remain available for acceptance until 12h00 on ___day of ____________, whereafter it shall lapse and be of no further force and effect.  The agents detailed on Page 2 “Contract Information – Selling Agents’” are hereby appointed as agents for the purpose of communication of acceptance.

14.	FIXTURES & FITTINGS

	The property is sold with all existing fixtures and fittings of a permanent nature and sold ‘voetstoots’ and which the Seller warrants are his exclusive property and fully paid for, including but not limited to:

	14.1	Fixed light fittings, fitted carpets and awnings;

	14.2	All fitted cupboards, shelving, curtain rails, rods and pelmets;

	14.3	Oven, Hob & Extractor;

	14.4	Free standing fireplace/heater;

	14.5	Pool filter, pump and cleaning equipment including automatic pool cleaner;

	14.6	Existing garden trees, shrubs, plants, garden irrigation and related equipment;

	14.7	Alternate power systems – invertor, batteries, solar panels;

	14.8	Water tanks; and 

	14.9	Burglar alarm systems, keys and remote controls for the property.

15.	CERTIFICATES OF COMPLIANCE (DELETE or state whichever is NOT APPLICABLE)

15.1 ELECTRICAL  

The SELLER shall, at its cost, deliver to the PURCHASER on or before the transfer date a certificate of compliance in regard to the electrical installation on the property in terms of the regulations made by the Minister of Manpower on 23rd October 1992 under Section 35 of the Machinery and Occupational Safety Act No 6 of 1983 and under Act 85 or 1993.  The SELLER undertakes not to alter the electrical installation after the issue of the said Certificate.

15.2	BEETLE FREE CERTIFICATE (ENTOMOLOGIST REPORT)

The Parties agree that, prior to transfer of the Property into the name of the Purchaser, the SELLER shall, at his expense, have all the accessible timbers of the property inspected by a SAPCA - registered Inspector for the infestation by Wood-destroying beetles, termites and fungi and a written report with recommendations shall be given to the SELLER. Where infestation is found, the recommendations made shall be carried out in full, in terms of Act 36 of 1947 and/or SANS Codes 0124 and 0204.  Upon receipt of a Certificate of Clearance issued by the said Inspector to the SELLER, to the effect that there is no apparent infestation on first inspection, or that any infestation which had been reported has been dealt with as set out above, the SELLER shall have fairly discharged all responsibility in the matter and the PURCHASER shall have no further claim against the SELLER.

15.3	GAS INSTALLATIONS

The SELLER shall, prior to the Occupation Date or Transfer of the Property, whichever is the earlier, furnish the PURCHASER with a valid certificate of conformity applicable to all gas appliances or systems on the property as prescribed in Regulation 17(3) of the Occupational Health and Safety Act.  The certificate will be issued by an authorised person registered as such with the Liquefied Petroleum Gas Safety Association of Southern Africa (LPGAS).  All expenses incurred in meeting the criteria for the issue of such certificate, including the certificate itself, shall be borne by the SELLER.  The SELLER furthermore warrants to the PURCHASER that no addition or alteration to the gas installations on the property has been effected since the issue of such certificate.  Upon the SELLER furnishing the PURCHASER with the said certificate of conformity, the PURCHASER shall have no claim whatsoever against the SELLER and no further liability in this regard shall rest upon the SELLER.

15.4	ELECTRIC FENCE

The Seller shall obtain at his cost the required Electric Fence System Certificate as mentioned in Regulation 12 of the Electrical Machinery Regulations, 2011 promulgated in terms of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 1983 (Act No 6 of 1983) in respect of the electric fence system and deliver the said Electric Fence System Certificate to the Purchaser within 15 days of acceptance of this offer by the Seller.  If the electric fence system on the premises is faulty, the Seller shall at his cost repair the electrical fence system in order to deliver the required Electric Fence System Certificate to the Purchaser.  The Seller undertakes not to make any alterations to the Electric Fence System after the issue of the certificate.  If the certificate has not been delivered within the period referred to above, the Purchaser shall be entitled but not obliged to obtain an Electric Fence System Certificate in respect of such system at his own costs and the conveyancer is hereby irrevocably instructed to pay to the Purchaser from the proceeds of the sale, on the date of registration of transfer of the Property into the name of the Purchaser, the costs incurred by the Purchaser of obtaining such Electric Fence System Certificate (including the costs of effecting any rectifications or repairs to enable the relevant party to issue such certificate).”

15.5	SOLAR SYSTEMS

The Seller shall obtain at his cost the required Certificate of Compliance (“COC”) as mentioned in Regulation 9 promulgated in terms of the Occupational Health and Safety Act No 85 of 1993.  The COC shall be issued by a Registered Person.  If a Solar System forms part of the electrical installations on the Property, it shall specifically be included in the COC which must be signed by an installation electrician or master installation electrician or an electric tester under the supervision of an installation electrician or master installation electrician.  If the electrical installation is faulty, the Seller shall at his cost repair the electrical installation.  The COC shall be delivered to the Purchaser within 15 days of the acceptance of the offer or fulfilment of the suspensive conditions (whichever is the later) and no alterations shall be affected after the issuing of the COC.

16.	INSPECTION

The PURCHASER has personally inspected the property and hereby accepts to purchase the property “Voetstoots” as it now stands.  The PURCHASER hereby waives any right to claim damages and/or costs for any such repairs on the property, whether caused by patent or latent defects. The SELLER hereby warrants that he has disclosed all known defects on the property including those listed on the Disclosure Report by the Seller attached hereto.

17.	CAPACITY OF PARTIES 

17.1	Should the PURCHASER sign this Agreement as agent for a company, close corporation or other juristic person to be formed, the signatory shall be deemed to be personally liable in terms of this Agreement should the company, close corporation or juristic person not be incorporated or formed or not ratify and adopt this Agreement within 30 (THIRTY) days of the date of signature hereof.  Upon formation or incorporation or ratification as aforesaid, the PURCHASER by his signature hereto binds himself as surety for and co-principal debtor in solidum with the company, close corporation or other juristic person or entity for the due and punctual performance by the company, close corporation or other juristic person or entity of its obligations arising out of this Agreement.

17.2 In the event of any of the parties to this Agreement being a company, close corporation, trust or other juristic person or entity, the person who signs this Agreement in the name or on behalf of such company, close corporation, trust or other juristic person or entity hereby warrants that such legal entity is indeed duly registered in terms of the applicable legislation and warrants that he is duly authorized to act for and/or on behalf of such legal entity, and he hereby binds himself as surety and co-principal debtor with such juristic person or entity in favour of the SELLER for all the obligations of such juristic person or entity in terms of this Agreement.  Such signatory shall be personally liable as PURCHASER or SELLER (as the case may be) in terms of this Agreement if such juristic person or entity legally does not exist and/or for whatsoever reason is not bound to this Agreement and/or fails to comply with any of the provisions hereof.

18.	SIGNATURE IN COUNTERPARTS

This Agreement of Sale may be signed in separate counterparts, each of which shall be deemed to be an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one and the same agreement. A counterpart of this Offer to Purchase in email form shall be conclusive evidence of the original signature and shall be as effective in law as the counterparts in original form showing the original signatures.

19.	BUILDING PLANS 

19.1	The SELLER confirms that he is in possession of all approved municipal building plans relating to the improvements erected on the Property ("as-built plans") and has provided the PURCHASER with copies thereof prior to the signing of this Agreement. The PURCHASER acknowledges receipt of the plans and hereby confirms that they are satisfied with the documentation provided. 

OR

19.1	The SELLER confirms that Municipal building plans for all or part of the existing improvements are not presently available and has disclosed this to the PURCHASER. The SELLER undertakes at their own risk to obtain all required Municipal approvals and approved building plans on or before date of registration and transfer of the property, and should the SELLER fail to procure such approvals within this time limit prior to transfer, the Conveyancer is irrevocably authorised and instructed to retain the sum of R100,000 (One Hundred Thousand Rand) (“the retained amount”) from the SELLER’s proceeds of the sale, to be held in trust pending compliance with the SELLER’s obligations under this clause. Upon the SELLER furnishing proof that the required approvals and plans have been obtained, the retained amount shall be released to the SELLER. If the SELLER has not obtained the required approvals within 3 (three) months from date of transfer of the property, the retained amount shall be paid to the PURCHASER without prejudice to any further rights or remedies the PURCHASER may have in law under this agreement.

20	ARBITRATION

20.1If any dispute, difference or question arises at any time between the parties out of or in regard to any matters arising out of, or the rights and duties of any of the parties, or the interpretation of, or termination of, or any matter arising out of the termination of, or the rectification of this agreement, such dispute shall be submitted to and decided by arbitration on notice given by either party to the other of them in terms of this paragraph.

20.2Such arbitration shall be held in Knysna in accordance with the provisions of the Arbitration Act No 42 of 1965 (as amended) save that the arbitration shall be informal and the arbitrator shall have the absolute discretion to determine the procedure to be adopted, it being the intention that the arbitration shall be held and concluded without delay.

20.3	The arbitrator shall be such independent or suitably qualified person as may be agreed upon between the parties in writing, and failing such agreement, the arbitrator shall be appointed by the President for the time being of the Law Society of the Cape of Good Hope or its successor/s at the request of either party.

20.4	The contents of Arbitration clause is severable from the rest of this agreement and shall remain in force notwithstanding the termination of this agreement for whatever reason.

23.	CONTINUED MARKETING

	The SELLER may continue to market the Property until the fulfilment of the suspensive conditions contained herein is fulfilled.  Should the SELLER, during this time, receive another more acceptable offer to purchase the Property, he will have the right to notify the PURCHASER, in writing, to waive or fulfil all suspensive conditions pertaining to his offer, and therefore making this sale unconditional, within 3 (three) working days of the date when such notice is delivered to the PURCHASER, or such extended period as the SELLER may allow.  Such notice to the PURCHASER shall include a copy of the competing offer.  If the PURCHASER fails to waive his rights or advise the SELLER that the suspensive conditions have been fulfilled, in writing within the waiver period, the SELLER shall be entitled to accept the competing offer and this sale shall lapse and be null and void.  Should the SELLER elect not to accept the competing offer, this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect.

24.	SUSPENSIVE CONDITIONS

	This Agreement of Sale is subject to the following suspensive conditions, failing which this Agreement shall be of no further force and effect. OR

	This Agreement is subject to the approval of the Master of the High Court of South Africa (Western Cape) for the sale and transfer of the property to the Purchaser.  Should such consent not be obtained or should the Master of the Supreme Court decline for any reason to furnish a certificate in terms of Section 42(2) of the Administration of Estates Act 66 of 1965, then this agreement shall lapse and be null and void.  The Purchasers acknowledge that they are aware that the Seller acts in a fiduciary capacity as Executor of a Deceased Estate and that the sale shall take place in accordance with their powers and authority in their capacity as such.
